messages.subject: How do I set the sum of the parameters to be 1?
parts:
Hi, 

I use three parameters, and the sum of the three parameters should be 1.
(e.g. alpha + beta + gamma = 1)

How do I set the sum of the parameters to be 1?

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: How do I set the sum of the parameters to be 1?
parts:
On Thursday, 23 March 2017 09:00:54 UTC, YeoChan Yoon wrote:
Hi, 

I use three parameters, and the sum of the three parameters should be 1.
(e.g. alpha + beta + gamma = 1)

How do I set the sum of the parameters to be 1?

In version 2.1, you can define your parameters with a range [0,1]. Then in your target-runner (or in your target-algorithm if you can modify that), simply divide each parameter value by their sum. The downside of this is that irace will handle configurations that map to the same parameter values as different (because the transformation done by your target-runner is not visible to irace). This may lead to some redundancy in some cases.

In the next version 2.2, there will be an option to specify repair mechanisms so that irace will only see the "repaired" configurations.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.author: 1e8700780c0e6d69
messages.subject: Re: How do I set the sum of the parameters to be 1?
parts:
Hello YeoChan, 

I just saw that Manuel posted too. The only way of doing this for now is to define parameters and then convert:

alpha    "--a " r  (0,1)
beta      "--b " r  (0,1)  
gamma      "--g " r  (0,1) 

In the targetRunner (hookRun) then you would need to compute the value of the parameters based on the selected numbers:
finalalpha =  alpha / (alpha + beta + gamma)
finalbeta =  beta / (alpha + beta + gamma)
finalgamma =  gamma / (alpha + beta + gamma)


Cheers!
Leslie.
